result:
**Bottom line: freeze after listed changes.** I had no tools and saw no engine; every "I derive" below is hand-checked against PB10's counts (which my derivations reproduce) and is unrefereed.

Three facts I use throughout:

- **F1. COPY-LAW(t) and FBP(t) are one law in arm 1.** With no taking rule a birth's distinct inputs equal its parents (FD 2.7 says so). Arm 1 has six base laws, not nine; every "COPY-LAW and FBP" count is doubled (68, 16, 52, 60, 4, 4, 440, 348, 116 are all even).
- **F2. The roster statement.** With no taking rule and RELEASE, the roster after a round, up to "the same" and with descent marks, depends only on the roster before it. New knots meet only their parents, so new met sets are sets of one parent's children; old met sets persist only among members that wait. I think it also holds under HOLD. Under parity it holds apart from the closing, which looks at loose and barred distinctions outside the roster. SD's end operator may already state it; check the record.
- **F3. A joined start is one start roster with its members marked X or Y.** One-2 J1 or J2 two-22 is the same roster as pairs-3 alone; two-22 J1 two-22 as pairs-4; one-2 J1 one-2 as two-22; one-2 J3 or J4 two-22 as three-222. The traced case is three-222 alone under not-all-equal, with marks.

## 1. The claim

- **Every member descended from both:** keep; report mixed parts apart, as D 3.1 does. Say plainly that after the first births with a parent in each, descent from both is nearly automatic, so it shows little.
- **Ended as a condition:** keep it for Y and report X. Add how they ended: every usable loose distinction given to births, or barred (retiring), or closed. Barred is not his "consume".
- **(a) and (b) are one condition under J1 to J3.** With X barred the roster is Y alone's (F2), and neither run can close under parity. Only J4 differs, because its dead knot keeps all of Y in one met set.
- **(c) is fair with any descent.** Two parts of Y's form without Y going in defeat "input" whoever made them. Report them by descent.
- **A condition is missing:** B(i) is listed in DB 3.6 and used nowhere. Add (d): with Y barred (X alone), fewer than two parts of Y's form.
- **"X comes out again" reported only:** right. Split "from X only" (SD's "returns") from "from both".
- **The whole-class CB fails under FLOOR1 by Settled 2 alone.** For any X at least five non-control members cannot be descended from both. It is a check, not a prediction.
- **What is actually tested under FLOOR1:** the single-member reading. Two-22 fails (b) by PB10 under every treatment. One-2 fails (b) under offshoots and waiting, and passes under CANCEL-RETIRE (0 for ever, by F2 and the cycle). So the one open case is Y = one-2 under FLOOR1 with CANCEL-RETIRE. Have it listed and traced.
- **As I would state it, in two readings:**
  - **CB-1 (Y with X):** under law L, run A has at some round t two parts the same as Y's form, each descended from both; the knots descended from Y only have ended by t; and fewer than two such parts (any descent) appear at every round read with X barred, in Y alone, and in X alone.
  - **CB-2 (X for the class):** CB-1 for every member other than the control, and not of the others (c).
  - **Standing:** CB-2 is settled false under FLOOR1 with no taking rule and under MET with COPY-LAW. It is open, and predicted to fail, under CAP-3 and under MET with FBP. CB-1 is predicted to fail everywhere, with the one-2 retiring case named.

## 2. The renaming argument

- **Order of births and names of new knots:** sound. Which births are made is read from h, k, met sets and counts.
- **Which loose distinction goes to which birth:** sound. Two allocations differ by a permutation of one member's usable loose distinctions, which fixes every knot. A member's offshoots are exchanged with it, with equal demand.
- **HOLD:** sound. The number kept is the number of cancelled groups; which are kept is the same permutation.
- **IMPLIED:** sound, and it can be sharpened. With at most two holders, a birth is implied exactly when it takes every loose distinction of its connected structure, with none barred there. The test is against the structure before the round, so order does not enter.
- **CAP-3's demand:** sound; it is read on the roster of new and kept members.
- **Joins of three or more:** sound; one join per group, named by its parent set.
- **The statement is false as written.** "σ_t agrees with σ on the start's knots and distinctions" fails. Counterexample: a start member holding loose a before b, making one join and one offshoot; σ exchanges the names of a and b. In S the join takes a; in σ(S) it takes σ(b). So σ_1 carries a to σ(b).
- **Repair:** σ_t agrees with σ on knots and on distinctions shared or barred at the start; on each member's usable loose distinctions only up to a permutation. Harmless for ticket B, since nothing reads a start distinction by name; it would matter for a values reading.
- **Verdict:** a proof once restated, and once it says the guard and T are counts. No counterexample to the substance.
- **The check:** 656 comparisons by hash cannot confirm sameness. Require exact comparison, or call those "not refuted". Add two renamings: two loose distinctions of one member exchanged, and one that changes the order of groups.

## 3. The narrowing arguments

- **Settled 2 is right, and it also holds under HOLD.** It uses only three facts: fresh is at most two, h never increases, and a birth takes only its parents' loose distinctions. Drop the caveat and keep the swap as the check.
- **Settled 3 is right, given S4.**
- **Open after Settled 2:** one-2 and two-22 under FLOOR1 for the single-member reading (see 1); everything under CAP-3.
- **Open after Settled 3:** MET under CAP-3, and **MET under FBP(t)**. D 1.6 registered FBP exactly because S4 fails there. Arm 2 omits it; add it.

## 4. A reason, or a census

- **(a) Per birth, your statement is right.** f depends on p (FLOOR1) or on p and demand (CAP-3), with no taking rule.
- **As a statement about what is left, it is wrong.** Y's form is carried whole for a round: h and the groups fix how many joins and offshoots there are and which share a parent, and children of one parent are joinable. Nothing forces Y to be forgotten.
- **The "almost"** is the joinable relation (through sets of one parent's children), shortness, demand under CAP-3, and the closing.
- **The reason that does hold** is F2 with Settled 2. Under FLOOR1 a made part whose members all hold two is one-2 or two-22, whatever went in. Once run A's roster is the same as some alone-run's roster, the two stay the same round for round. The traced case reaches a lone member holding two at round 3 and is one-2 alone from there.
- **Under CAP-3 there is no reason, only a census.**
- **(b) Yes, register it, reported, with a prediction.**
- **(c) Stated so it is decidable:**
  - For each X, law, way and knot law, list per round the forms of parts descended from both, with counts, for each Y.
  - R1: the number of distinct such lists across the eight Y.
  - R2: a form is specific to Y when it is descended from both with Y and at no round read with any other Y′.
  - R3: the first round after which run A's whole roster is the same as an alone-run's roster at some round, and which one.
- **Prediction:** the lists differ with Y in counts and rounds (not constant); R2 is empty; under FLOOR1 the forms present twice are two-22, its next-round form and one-2.
- **Not over-read:** it holds for this class, these ways and these rounds; do not write "nearly the same" without counts.

## 5. Arm 1's standing

- **Register it as a census** with three settled statements (renaming, F2, Settled 2) and the bounded predictions. Do not register it as a claim that could be "made".
- **Say F3 in the text**, with a table of each joined start's round-0 roster form and which starts are the same.
- **The class is not fair as a test of FLOOR1.** Six of eight kinds are excluded by argument under one of the two rations (F1).
- **A fair class, per law:** the forms that law makes as parts with every member made, taken from the alone runs and fixed from the disclosed scratch lists (say that it is post hoc). Keep the eight kinds as the registered list beside it.
- **Optional:** by F2, a made part the same as a joined start's roster behaves as that start. A search of the record's runs for such parts would say whether any arm-1 meeting is ever made.

## 6. Arm 2

- **Keep it as an arm:** it is the only place a case can be "made".
- **Its laws:** MET under CAP-3(t) and FBP(t). MET with COPY-LAW becomes one check row (PB3).
- **Say that arm 2 gives back the numbering:** takes use names, so every case needs D 4.5's renamings.

## 7. The knot law deciding the traced case

- **Not a finding.** It is SD's closing exception: the join of three takes every loose distinction there is.
- **Register a check instead:** with no taking rule, runs under the two knot laws are identical until a closing. Report the runs that close.
- **Like for like:** Y alone (e barred) and B_X can never close, while run A can. Say so wherever (a) and (b) are read under parity.

## 8. The definitions

- **s:** DB 3.1 and 3.6 fix s = 0, but arm 2's made designs have s = 1. Use the design's s.
- **The round:** DB 4.1 needs one t with two of Y from both after t and the knots descended from Y only ended by t. "That round" in DB 3.5 should be the first such t; "exactly two" is read at that t.
- **(b):** "members made after round 0" does not say every member or some member. Use any descent at t ≥ 1, as (a) and (c).
- **One-member kinds:** say that a part the same as one-2 is a member holding two, k = 0, joinable with none.
- **J2 and J3 on pairs-3 and pairs-4:** "X's dead knot" is ambiguous; name the first.
- **First member:** say which member of two-23 is first.
- **The last-member swap is nearly empty.** For every kind but two-23 the last member is exchanged with the first by a renaming (up to which dead knot holds e), so Settled 1 predicts the same run. Replace it with a member not exchanged with the first: the other member of two-23, and a member in two met sets for pairs-3 and pairs-4.
- **e:** "its swap: the other knot law" is not a swap. In run A the joined start is already one connected structure, so e does not change the closing; it does change the knot test and gives z a third place. Either register starts without e where z keeps three places, or say e has no swap.
- **Scaffolds without a run:** the class, the bounds and the labels are listed with swaps that B2 does not make. Name the run or say "no swap".
- **Alone runs:** X alone is undefined in DB, though X's form and (d) need it. Y alone for pairs kinds must name all its dead knots.
- **Joint birth:** by FD's letter an offshoot of a knot descended from both is a joint birth. For DB 6, define the first joint births: one parent descended from X only and one from Y only.
- **T:** say what is reported when a comparison run stops before run A's case ("not compared").
- **"In standard terms":** "isomorphic as a labelled component" overstates. The reading is "the same" on h, k and maximal met sets.
- **Six rounds is too few.** The traced case appears at round 6, the last one. Read at least 8 rounds, 10 under CAP-3, and raise the guard to match.

## 9. The predictions

- **True by construction, mark as check:** PB4 for the whole class under FLOOR1; PB8 under COPY-LAW (it is PB3); PB11 for arm 1 (two holders, fresh or closing; cite the ring study's settled statement); (a) the same as (b) under J1 to J3; F1.
- **Replication only:** PB10 (it is the prototype's counts, not "true by construction"; keep it as the engine's control); PB6; PB1's sentence on MET.
- **Undecidable as registered:** PB1 where compared by hash; PB6 if ticket A's output does not yet exist (say which output).
- **Over-pinned:** PB7's "seen" forms and PB9's counts are doubled by F1; restate them on six laws.
- **Expected to fail as worded:** PB1 if "agrees on distinctions" is tested literally; PB10 if the helper reads "members made after round 0" differently.
- **Missing:**
  - F1 and F2 as checks.
  - The table of round-0 roster forms (F3).
  - The reading of 4(c).
  - Condition (d).
  - MET under FBP.
  - The one-2 retiring case, listed.
  - Whether each failure is by argument or by census.
  - A named weighting for "85 to 97 percent of small starts", "nearly any" and "almost any".

## 10. The inkling and autocatalysis

- I have not seen A248's text. Keeping it apart from the evidence is right.
- **Over-read:** "a failure supports his first sentence". Where the failure is by Settled 2 or 3 it is a fact about the ration, not about patterns. Mark each failure "by argument" or "by census", and let only the census ones bear on the inkling.
- **The autocatalysis reading is fair, and the claim should name it** (from memory, not checked: A + B → 2B, with B the one that increases). His sentence, read literally, is CB-1, Y becoming two of itself only with X. CB-2 adds (c) and is the thread's stricter reading. Report both, so that failure of the strict one is not all he hears.

## 12. The seven questions

1. Every member from both; mixed reported apart.
2. A condition for Y, with how they ended; the reported-only version stays as its swap.
3. Any descent; add (d).
4. A census with settled statements (see 5).
5. Do not add it to the class. It is the two-knot part one round on, and it becomes two of itself alone. Say so under PB7 and check it.
6. No more scratch runs before the freeze. Register 10 rounds under CAP-3, the per-law class and the reading of 4(c), and say "computed, bounded".
7. Yes (see 10).

## 13. Scope and honesty

- **The sentence as I would write it:**

  > "We tried it your way: the first and second pattern start as one part, and what is left descends from both. With no rule for taking shared distinctions, the outcome cannot depend on how the start is numbered; that is proved, and it is new. But the meeting then has to be built into the start, and a start built so is one start pattern with its members marked first or second. Under the ration under which the two-knot part copies itself, two parts of the second pattern's form are left only when that form is the two-knot part or a lone member holding two; the ration cannot leave any other form of our list, by argument. In every run seen those two are also left without the first pattern, so nothing was needed from it. Under the cap of three no two parts of the second pattern's form were seen, through the rounds run; nothing is argued there. Under the taking rule that lets parts meet, none was seen either, and under one ration none is possible."

- **The draft's "under the cap of three nothing comes out twice" is false against PB7**, where the controls leave two parts of the growing form.
- **Blurs of law and pattern:**
  - "the ration of the part that copies itself" gives a ration to a part.
  - "X and Y meet" in arm 1, where they are one part from round 0 and X, Y are marks on a start.
  - "the law makes those two forms from nearly any start" is fine once the weighting is named.
